items.evidence: "by" is used with deadlines to mean not later than a certain time.
An adverb ("efficiently") is required to modify the verb "works".
Modal verb "must" is followed by the base form of the verb ("register").
"since" is used with the present perfect tense to indicate a starting point in time.
The noun "discount" follows the indefinite article "a".
"because" introduces a clause explaining the reason for the postponement.
The verb "encourage" in the passive structure takes an infinitive with "to".
The possessive determiner "our" is followed by a plural noun ("requirements").
First conditional sentence uses present simple in the if-clause and future simple ("will inspect") in the main clause.
Past time marker "yesterday" combined with passive voice requires "were reviewed".
The verb "contact" requires an object pronoun ("me").
"near" functions as a preposition meaning close to.
The phrasal prepositional phrase "look forward to" is followed by a gerund ("seeing").
An adverb ("carefully") modifies the past participle "checked".
"by" indicates the amount or degree of change ("increased by ten percent").
Superlative form "fastest" is required after "the" when comparing routes.
"for" is used with a period of time ("two years").
Subject "Every applicant" is singular and takes a singular verb in the present tense ("needs").
"in case" means as a precaution against a possible event or situation.
Past participle "damaged" functions as an adjective modifying the noun "component".
